_meta.purpose: Real-world precedent for grounding EVAL01 scenario parameters (config/benchmark/bab_el_mandeb.yaml + scenario YAMLs, once written) for the Bab el-Mandeb / Red Sea chokepoint, matching the structure and honesty conventions of data/routing_research/hormuz_rerouting_patterns.json. Documentation only — does not itself write or change any scenario YAML.
_meta.labeling: Each numeric value carries an evidence tag: 'documented' (a cited source states the number) or 'extrapolated' (derived/interpolated — the derivation is recorded in that event's 'notes'). A null value is a correct result when no credible source was found; it is explained, not guessed.
_meta.units_convention: Per docs/multiregion/BENCHMARK_SCHEMA_REFERENCE.md: the EVAL01 pipeline's 'shipping' signal is a raw vessel-transit count/day; 'market' is an unbounded, roughly z-score-like index; 'geopolitical'/'routing'/'news'/'disaster' are 0-1 normalized scores. The values recorded below are the real-world documented quantities in their own natural units (percent, USD, nautical miles, incident counts) — mapping any of them onto the pipeline's internal 0-1/raw-count convention is scenario-authoring work for a later prompt, not done here.

events.name: 2023-2024 Houthi Red Sea shipping attack campaign

shipping.unit: % year-over-year decline in Suez Canal vessel transit count, 2024 vs 2023 (13,213 ships in 2024 vs ~26,434 in 2023)

value.baseline_pre_crisis_estimate: roughly a third of the Feb 2024 peak, per 'tripled' framing in source

market.unit: USD per FEU (forty-foot equivalent unit), Asia-Europe container spot freight rate

geopolitical.unit: cumulative documented Houthi attack incidents on shipping, Nov 2023 - mid 2024

disaster.explanation: No natural-hazard driver applies to this event. This is a security/geopolitical campaign, not a natural disaster — structurally analogous to Hormuz's P_CRIT/P_HIGH scenarios, where the disaster domain stays enabled-but-silent (effect: null) throughout a geopolitical/blockage event.

routing.unit: % of 7,500+ TEU vessels rerouted via Cape of Good Hope; nautical miles / days added per voyage

news.unit: n/a — no direct sentiment/volume index found
news.explanation: No published news-sentiment or article-volume index specific to this campaign was located in this research pass. The cumulative-incident-count trajectory (1 incident 2023-11-19, ramping to 100+ by mid-2024, per the geopolitical field above) is a plausible proxy for the shape of a news-volume ramp, but is not itself a measured news signal — treat any use of it as extrapolated, not documented.

events.notes: Escalation timeline (documented): 2023-11-19 Galaxy Leader seized near Hodeida (opening incident); 2023-12-14 missile near-misses Maersk Gibraltar; 2023-12-15 Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd suspend Red Sea transits; 2023-12-16/17 MSC and CMA CGM follow. War-risk premiums (from a separate strand of the same search pass, not independently re-verified against a single primary source here) rose from ~0.07% of hull value pre-crisis to as high as 2% by mid-2024 — recorded for context but not entered as a signal_effects field since Hormuz's own war-risk-premium precedent (data/routing_research/hormuz_rerouting_patterns.json, 2019 event) already establishes this quantity's role for the routing/market domains and this file avoids duplicating that derivation. 'shipping' uses the Suez Canal aggregate transit count as a proxy for Bab el-Mandeb transits specifically, because virtually every vessel that transits Bab el-Mandeb northbound continues directly into the Suez Canal within the same days-long voyage leg — the two chokepoints' transit counts move together almost 1:1 for this event, unlike Hormuz where the destination chokepoint IS the endpoint. This proxy relationship should be stated explicitly wherever this file is used to ground a scenario parameter, not treated as a literal Bab el-Mandeb-specific measurement.

events.name: 2025-2026 pause and February 2026 resumption

shipping.unit: % below corresponding 2023 (pre-crisis) weekly Suez Canal transit level, as of early January 2026, despite ~100 days without a confirmed Houthi attack

market.explanation: No specific freight-rate figure for this sub-window was located; only the traffic-recovery shortfall above was documented.

geopolitical.value: attacks resumed following 2026-02-28 US/Israeli strikes on Iran

disaster.explanation: Not applicable — same reasoning as the 2023-2024 event.

routing.explanation: A specific reroute-percentage figure for this sub-window was not located; only the aggregate traffic-recovery shortfall (shipping field above) was documented.

news.explanation: Not independently sourced for this sub-window.

events.notes: IMPORTANT CROSS-REGION LINK: the 2026-02-28 US/Israeli strikes on Iran that reignited this campaign are the SAME trigger event as this thesis's own pinned Hormuz ground-truth disruption, documented in data/routing_research/hormuz_rerouting_patterns.json under '2026_hormuz_closure' (onset 2026-02-28, matching shipping_connector.py's _KNOWN_SHUTDOWN_START/_END). Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz scenarios grounded in this shared window are not independent events — a multi-region benchmark run spanning both should account for this correlation (e.g. a P_CRIT scenario for one region co-occurring with elevated risk in the other is realistic, not an artifact). The pause itself (2025-11-11 to ~2026-02-28, ~3.5 months) shows traffic recovers only partially and slowly even after a sustained attack-free period (60% below baseline after 100 attack-free days) — worth preserving as a 'recovery is asymmetric and slow' finding distinct from Hormuz, where no comparable multi-month calm-then-still-depressed period has been documented in this pass.

limitations: (1) Bab el-Mandeb-specific transit-count figures, independent of the Suez Canal aggregate, were not found in this pass; the Suez proxy relationship is noted explicitly above and should not be treated as a literal Bab el-Mandeb measurement. (2) No natural-disaster driver exists for this region's documented disruption history within this research scope — the region's risk profile in this file is entirely geopolitical/security, which should be reflected by declining to invent a disaster scenario class for bab_el_mandeb rather than forcing one. (3) A specific 'news' sentiment/volume index was not located for either event; any news-domain scenario parameter grounded in this file is extrapolated from incident-count timing, not a measured news signal. (4) War-risk insurance premium figures were found (0.07% to ~2% of hull value) but not cross-verified against a second independent primary source within this pass, and were deliberately left out of signal_effects to avoid presenting a single-source figure as more solid than it is — a future pass wanting a market-domain war-risk-premium number should re-verify this figure first. (5) The 2025-2026 sub-window is thinner than the 2023-2024 campaign: several signal_effects fields are null because a focused, quantified secondary-source search for that narrower window was not exhaustive.
